policies.label: MRI lumbar spine without contrast
policies.source_note: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0236: MRI and CT of the Spine. Criteria quoted from the policy; red flags are the stand-alone indications that do not require a conservative-therapy trial.

criteria.text: Low back pain with radiculopathy: radicular leg pain in a nerve root (dermatomal) distribution.
criteria.question_if_missing: Does the patient have radiating leg pain in a nerve root distribution, for example pain going below the knee into the calf or foot?

criteria.text: Pain plus objective findings of motor or reflex changes in the specific nerve root distribution.
criteria.question_if_missing: On exam, were there objective neurological findings such as a diminished or absent reflex, motor weakness, or sensory loss in a specific nerve root distribution?

criteria.text: No improvement after 6 weeks of conservative therapy (conservative therapy = moderate activity, analgesics, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, muscle relaxants).
criteria.question_if_missing: How many weeks of conservative therapy has the patient completed, such as NSAIDs, analgesics, muscle relaxants, activity modification, or physical therapy, and over what dates?

criteria.text: Clinical suspicion of a spinal cord or cauda equina compression syndrome (e.g., saddle anesthesia, new bowel or bladder dysfunction, urinary retention, bilateral leg weakness).
Rapidly progressing neurological deficit, or major motor weakness.
Suspected infectious process (e.g., osteomyelitis, epidural abscess of the spine or soft tissue), such as back pain with fever or intravenous drug use.
Primary spinal bone tumors or suspected vertebral, paraspinal, or intraspinal metastases (e.g., new back pain with a history of cancer or unexplained weight loss).
Suspected spinal fracture and/or dislocation secondary to trauma (if plain films are not conclusive).

policies.label: MRI knee (lower extremity joint) without contrast
policies.source_note: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0171: MRI of the Extremities (knee section), last reviewed 03/31/2026.

criteria.text: Persistent knee pain, swelling, and/or instability (giving way).
criteria.question_if_missing: Is the patient's knee pain persistent, and is there swelling or instability such as the knee giving way?

criteria.text: Not responding to at least 3 weeks of conservative therapy (conservative therapy consists of a combination of rest, ice, compression, elevation, plus NSAIDs and/or physical therapy).
criteria.question_if_missing: What conservative treatment has the patient tried for the knee, such as rest, ice, NSAIDs, bracing or physical therapy, and for how many weeks, with approximate start and end dates?

criteria.text: Multi-view x-rays have been obtained and have ruled out a fracture or loose body in the knee.
criteria.question_if_missing: Were plain x-rays of the knee obtained, and did they rule out a fracture or loose body?

criteria.text: Persistent true locking of the knee indicative of a torn meniscus or loose body (more than a momentary locking of the joint with the knee in a flexed position).
Suspected bone infection (i.e., osteomyelitis) or septic joint.
Detection, staging, and post-treatment evaluation of tumor of the knee.

policies.label: Polysomnography, attended in-lab (6+ hours)
policies.source_note: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0004: Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Adults. Attended in-lab NPSG is covered when symptoms suggest OSA and a listed condition makes home testing inappropriate.

criteria.text: Symptoms suggestive of obstructive sleep apnea: excessive daytime sleepiness and at least two of the following three: loud snoring, witnessed apneas or choking/gasping during sleep, diagnosed hypertension.
criteria.question_if_missing: Does the patient have excessive daytime sleepiness, and which of the following are present: loud snoring, witnessed apneas or gasping during sleep, or a diagnosis of hypertension?

criteria.text: Super obesity (BMI greater than 45), or pulmonary function studies show obesity hypoventilation syndrome.
criteria.question_if_missing: What is the patient's current BMI, or height and weight?

criteria.text: Moderate to severe pulmonary disease (for example, COPD or asthma) requiring nocturnal oxygen, or daytime hypercapnia (pCO2 above 45) on blood gas.
criteria.question_if_missing: Does the patient have moderate to severe COPD or asthma requiring nocturnal oxygen, or documented daytime hypercapnia?

criteria.text: Neuromuscular disease, stroke with residual respiratory effects, epilepsy, congestive heart failure (NYHA class III or IV, or LVEF below 45%), pulmonary hypertension, or chronic opioid medication use.
criteria.question_if_missing: Does the patient have neuromuscular disease, prior stroke, epilepsy, congestive heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, or chronic opioid use?

criteria.text: A single home sleep apnea test was negative, inconclusive, or technically inadequate.
criteria.question_if_missing: Has the patient had a home sleep apnea test, and if so was it negative, inconclusive, or technically inadequate?

policies.label: Wegovy (semaglutide 2.4 mg) for chronic weight management — pharmacy PA, NDC 0169-4525-14, no CPT
policies.source_note: Cigna Weight Loss – GLP-1 Agonists Prior Authorization policy (CNF 684). The PDF was unreachable on 2026-10-11; criteria transcribed from Cigna's published summaries of the same policy (secondary source).

criteria.text: Individual is 18 years of age or older.
criteria.question_if_missing: How old is the patient?

criteria.text: Initial body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m2 or greater (obese), or 27 kg/m2 or greater (overweight) in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition.
criteria.question_if_missing: What was the patient's baseline BMI, or height and weight, at the start of treatment?

criteria.text: Weight-related comorbid condition documented (e.g., hypertension, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus, obstructive sleep apnea, cardiovascular disease). Required when BMI is 27 to 29.9.
criteria.question_if_missing: Does the patient have a weight-related comorbidity such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes, sleep apnea, or cardiovascular disease?

criteria.text: Documented participation in a comprehensive weight-management program including a reduced-calorie diet, increased physical activity, and behavioral modification for at least 3 months prior to the request.
criteria.question_if_missing: How long has the patient participated in a structured diet, exercise, and behavioral weight-management program, and when did it start?

criteria.text: The medication will be used as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity, and will not be used in combination with another GLP-1 agonist or weight-loss medication.
criteria.question_if_missing: Will Wegovy be used together with continued diet and exercise, and is the patient on any other GLP-1 or weight-loss medication?

policies.label: Therapeutic exercise (physical therapy), each 15 min
policies.source_note: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0325: Physical Therapy. 97110 is covered when the general PT selection criteria are met.

criteria.text: Physical therapy is intended to significantly improve, develop or restore physical functions lost or impaired as a result of a disease, injury or surgical procedure, with the functional loss documented by physical measures (e.g., range of motion, strength, gait, functional scale).
criteria.question_if_missing: What objective functional deficits were measured, such as range of motion, strength, gait or a functional outcome score?

criteria.text: PT must be provided in accordance with an ongoing, written plan of care of sufficient detail, including appropriate objective and subjective data, frequency, duration, and measurable goals.
criteria.question_if_missing: Is there a written plan of care with frequency, duration, and measurable goals, and what are they?

criteria.text: There must be a reasonable expectation that the member's condition will improve significantly in a reasonable and generally predictable period of time; therapy that is neither regressing nor improving (maintenance) is not covered.
criteria.question_if_missing: What is the expected improvement and over what time frame?

criteria.text: Services must be of the complexity and nature to require that they are performed by a licensed professional therapist (skilled need), not a home exercise program alone.
criteria.question_if_missing: Why does the patient require skilled therapist-delivered treatment rather than a home exercise program?

policies.label: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
policies.source_note: BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina CAM 717: CT Abdomen (and CT Abdomen/Pelvis), reviewed 02/18/2026. Ultrasound-first language applies to biliary, hepatic and pancreatic indications.

criteria.text: Clinical indication involves both the abdomen and pelvis (e.g., acute abdominal pain, widespread inflammatory disease, or neoplasm), so CT abdomen/pelvis (74176-74178) is the correct study rather than abdomen or pelvis alone.
criteria.question_if_missing: What is the clinical question, and does it involve both the abdomen and the pelvis?

criteria.text: Initial clinical evaluation is documented: recent pertinent office visit notes with physical exam and laboratory data (e.g., CBC, liver function tests, lipase, urinalysis).
criteria.question_if_missing: What laboratory work has been done, such as CBC, liver function tests, lipase or urinalysis, and what were the results?

criteria.text: For right upper quadrant pain with suspected biliary disease, jaundice, or abnormal liver function tests: ultrasound was performed first and was negative or equivocal. CT can be considered without prior ultrasound only when ultrasound is limited by body habitus/BMI or another guideline criterion is met.
criteria.question_if_missing: Has an abdominal ultrasound been performed? If yes, what did it show? If not, was there a reason it was skipped, such as body habitus?

criteria.text: Suspected acute surgical abdomen: peritoneal signs, suspected perforation, bowel obstruction, abscess, or hemodynamic instability.
Known or suspected malignancy requiring initial staging (CT abdomen and pelvis is the more appropriate study for initial staging of the majority of cancers).
